chapter: Players and bands of old New Orleans
title: The best dance bands and Perez's lineup
summary: He rates Buddy Petit, Joe Oliver and Manuel Perez's bands, and lists the players Perez kept around his son.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Which was the best band for the dance band in those days? The best band? No, the dance for the orchestra for the...

Well, the orchestra bands, I'm going to tell you, in them times, Buddy P.T. had a good go at one time. But he lost it, like I'm telling you, just like Rickard did, taking too many deposits. Yeah. They lost confidence in it. But he had a good band. They'd follow him anywhere he'd go. Yeah. Joe Oliver was the same way. He had a good band. He was here. Manuel Perez had a great band, playing upon the Pissian Temple.

He tried to do, make his son, put his son down on the trumpet, put him down in the band. But boy wouldn't do right. He wouldn't make good. He never did make good. He played, but he never did make good. He had to give it up. Yeah. But he kept him right there on the bandstand with him, playing with all good musicians. Cherie was playing clarinet, sax, Adolf Alexander was playing clarinet, sax. Martin was playing guitar. Saik was playing drums. Oh yeah, good lineup. He had a good lineup. I met all them fellas out to wait for the night. Even my friends.
